market_holds: Options: the event-implied move is 9.98% (front straddle 14.37%, ATM IV 69.1%, 25d skew +2.94 vol points toward puts, put/call OI 0.73), about twice the 5.09% median of the last 7 prints (max -17.75% in Nov 2025, on a Q1 revenue miss and weak Q2 outlook) [sealed baseline, 2026-11-24]. Tape: spot 55.33 at the 18:08 UTC seal, down 23.9% over 20 sessions, 25.9% below the 52-week high, and down about 5% intraday on the print day. Peer bars I pulled (Yahoo chart, 2026-11-24) put the move since Oct 27 mostly in the market: NTNX -25%, QQQ -11%, IGV -14%, NetApp -28%, Dell -40%, Super Micro -35%. The trigger was the post-midterm AI and data-centre selloff that peaked on Nov 5. Consensus is non-GAAP EPS about $0.60 on revenue of $761.8M (+13.6% y/y), slightly above the $755-765M guide midpoint; the EarningsWhispers whisper is $0.71 (preview of 2026-11-16). I found no sign that estimates moved after the selloff, so the de-rating came through the price, not the numbers. The FY27 guide of $3.18-3.23B, set on 2026-08-26, already assumes server supply constraints all year and more future-start-date deals. The stock trades on the guide and the start-date timing.
view: This is a stock that fell with its sector into a print whose fundamental bar has not moved. Nutanix beat the top of its Q4 revenue guide ($757.1M against a $745M high end) and beat every guided metric. It set Q1 at $755-765M, roughly flat on Q4, and an FY27 guide that already builds in server shortages, rising hardware prices and more future-start-date deals. A Q1 revenue beat looks likely on that pattern. The reaction will turn on Q2 and the FY guide. On the positive side, management has a history of conservative guides, Lenovo ISG revenue rose 178% (reported 2026-11-19), so server supply is flowing at a price, and a 25% drawdown driven mostly by the market lowers the bar for relief. On the negative side, the memory crunch looks worse than in August (a Team Group executive on 2026-11-02 put the worst between Q4 2026 and Q2 2027). The President and Chief Commercial Officer left effective Oct 2, inside the quarter's last month, with sales moving to the CEO, on top of a 5% layoff finishing by end-October. And last year's Q1 is the template for a start-date shift dragging the FY number. The options already price a move about twice the usual size with a downside lean. I found nothing that tells me which way the guide goes beyond what management told the market in August. The overnight tape after a 5% intraday drop in infrastructure names adds noise. I cannot see a directional edge.

recommendation.reason: The drawdown into the print is mostly market and sector beta (post-midterm AI/data-centre selloff), not a company datapoint, and consensus sits on the guide midpoint. Upside from a likely beat and a lowered price is balanced by real guide risk: memory shortages worse than in August, a mid-quarter departure of the head of sales, and last year's start-date template. I found no dated evidence that tells me which way the FY guide moves, so there is no mechanism to bet on.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A raised or held FY27 revenue guide with Q2 above about $806M (my rough +12% y/y bar) and no new commentary on future-start-date mix would make me lean long. An FY trim citing start dates or memory pricing would make me short.

self_critique: The case for long is that a stock de-rated 25% on market beta into a quarter where the company has beaten the top of its guide is set up for relief, and the whisper says buy-side expects a beat. The case for short is that last November was the same set-up (beat, then a start-date-driven FY trim, -17.75%). Memory pricing has worsened since the guide, and the sales leader left mid-quarter. Both are real and I could not weigh them with evidence the market lacks, so I hold near 50.
